A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TD-Paint, with matching authors, core formulation and main datasets. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original inpainting experiments on CelebA-HQ, ImageNet1K and Places2, including quality metrics, runtime, diversity, training-mask ablations and qualitative results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds evaluated latent-diffusion baselines and qualitative demonstrations using user-drawn masks.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 removes v1's explicit forward-noising assignment for the unknown region, previously line 6. This is a limited revision of the stated sampler; the pixel-wise conditioning, training loss and architecture equations remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish a corresponding implementation change.

E1.justification: v2 adds object- and region-aligned user-drawn mask scenarios on ImageNet1K and Places2 in Figures 24–25. The three datasets and six existing quantitative mask settings remain unchanged.

E2.justification: v2 Tables 1–2 add evaluated comparisons with LDM, ControlNet, Blended Latent Diffusion, Uni-paint and PowerPaint across all three datasets. LaMa/MAT quality comparisons are retained in Appendix C, but MAT is removed from the diversity comparison in v1 Table 5 versus v2 Table 4.

E3.justification: Added experiments specify training LDM and ControlNet with computational resources equivalent to TD-Paint, their differing conditioning inputs, and ImageNet class-name text for foundation models. The original resolution, test-set sizes, metrics, TD-Paint training budgets and runtime measurement procedure are retained.

E4.justification: Figures 24–25 add qualitative case studies testing practical object- and region-specific editing selections. The training-mask ablation in Appendix A and diffusion-step analyses in Appendix B are retained without substantive changes.

E5.justification: Neither version reports confidence intervals, significance tests or training-seed variability. The stated diversity sampling of ten generations for 100 inputs and averaging over 100 images in the diffusion-step analysis remain unchanged.

E6.justification: The added baselines produce substantial new scores and rankings: LDM's CelebA-HQ Expand KID is 0.00496 versus TD-Paint's retained 0.00710 in v2 Table 2. Existing Places2 results also change: TD-Paint Altern. Lines LPIPS/SSIM moves from 0.073/0.851 to 0.060/0.879 in Table 1. User-drawn-mask outputs are added, while MAT's diversity scores are removed.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(14), including the diffusion formulation, loss and pixel-wise time-conditioning mathematics, are retained. No new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs or substantive derivations appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims: pixel-wise time conditioning enables faster, high-quality and diverse inpainting without architectural changes, demonstrated on three datasets. The additional evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 adds explanations involving latent-mask downsampling, ControlNet's missing mask information, foundation-model backbones and ImageNet textual conditioning. It qualifies the previous large-mask KID superiority with the LDM exception on CelebA-HQ. The speed comparison is explicitly scoped to pixel-space models, and Appendix D discusses practical user-drawn selections.

D1.justification: v1's statement that code is supplied in supplementary materials is replaced by an explicit GitHub repository address. v2 also documents resource matching and conditioning inputs for the added LDM/ControlNet comparisons. Existing TD-Paint hyperparameters and hardware disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds cited works for Differential Diffusion, ControlNet, Blended Latent Diffusion, Uni-paint and PowerPaint. Section 2 newly distinguishes Differential Diffusion's noisy soft-inpainting from TD-Paint's clean conditioning, while retaining the original related-work organization and central novelty argument.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section ordering are retained. Changes include localized clarifications, author/header and citation-style edits, and relocation of the CNN/transformer comparison from Section 5.3 to Appendix C, with corresponding cross-reference updates.

P2.justification: The comparison displays are substantially reorganized: main figures emphasize diffusion baselines, CNN/transformer panels are separately displayed in the appendix, KID comparisons are split between tables, and qualitative galleries gain five comparator columns. Two user-drawn-mask figures are added, Figure 1's labels/caption are revised, and the document adopts the ICLR layout.

improvement.justification: Testing latent models that also receive contextual information addresses a comparison gap in v1 and makes TD-Paint's strengths and limits easier to assess. Practical mask examples and clearer code-access information also help. However, the retained consistent-outperformance wording conflicts with BLD's lower Wide/Narrow LPIPS in Table 1, and runtime evidence excludes the added comparators. These limitations temper the overall improvement.
